descriptionChirho: An adverb meaning 'downward,' 'below,' or 'beneath,' derived from the root נָטָה (to stretch, incline) with the locative ה ending. Frequently combined with prepositions: מִלְּמַטָּה 'from below' in the tabernacle construction (Exod 26:24; 27:5; 28:27; 36:29; 38:4; 39:20), לְמַטָּה 'downward' or 'below' in descriptions of spatial orientation (Deut 28:13; Jer 31:37; Ezra 9:13), and וּלְמַטָּה 'and downward' for age limits (1 Chr 27:23; Ezek 1:27; 8:2). Used figuratively in Prov 15:24 where the path of the wise leads upward, away from Sheol beneath. Also in the expression 'lower and lower' (Deut 28:43) and in Eccl 3:21 questioning whether the spirit of the beast goes downward to the earth.
